thread:
zoe: Hey team — customer sees 401s from the browser only when using our Edge TS SDK inside an iframe. Server-side (Node) requests work fine. Repro steps below, curious if this rings a bell.

zoe: Repro steps:
1) Next.js app deployed to Vercel (Edge runtime) with an iframe embedding a 3rd-party dashboard.
2) Client does fetch('/api/infer', { method: 'POST', credentials: 'include', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hello' }) })
3) Edge API route uses @redwood/inference-js/edge v0.8.1:
```js
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-js/edge'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
const res = await client.generate({ prompt })
```
4) Network shows initial request gets a 307 redirect, then final request returns 401. On the browser network tab the Authorization header is missing on the redirected request.
5) Server logs show: "request_id=abc123 route=/api/infer status=401 msg=missing-auth"

zoe: Notes: works fine when tested from a server-side cron (Node) against same model. Customer is on modern browsers with 3rd-party cookies blocked.

eng-kiana: Thanks Zoe — this looks like the old redirect+fetch behavior in some edge runtimes. SDK v0.8.x used a tiny fetch wrapper that unintentionally let redirects drop Authorization when follow happened inside the runtime polyfill. Two quick checks: 1) can you reproduce with the SDK bumped to 0.9.3? We shipped a fix that preserves Authorization across manual redirect handling; 2) as an immediate workaround, set fetch option `redirect: 'manual'` in your client proxy so the runtime doesn't follow and drop headers.

eng-kiana: Example workaround in the edge handler:
```js
const resp = await fetch(upstreamUrl, {
  method: req.method,
  headers: { ...req.headers },
  redirect: 'manual', // avoid runtime auto-follow that loses auth
  credentials: 'include'
})
if (resp.status === 307) {
  // follow manually and copy Authorization back
}
```

sam: Also confirm whether the browser preflight is including `authorization` in Access-Control-Request-Headers. If the preflight doesn't include it, the actual request won't send it. Check the network tab for the OPTIONS request and look at `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` on your response — the proxy must include `authorization` and `x-request-id` if you rely on them.

sam: Can you also paste the X-Request-Id from the failing request (zoe mentioned abc123)? I want to check routing in the infra logs to see if any gateway (Vercel/CF) mutated the headers.

zoe: Got it. X-Request-Id from client is abc123. Preflight shows Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type. Response from our API has Access-Control-Allow-Headers: content-type but not authorization. Aha.

support-bot: Created INC-20232 for this: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-20232 — assigned to eng-kiana and eng-runtime team.

lara: Quick recommended fix steps for the customer:
- bump @redwood/inference-js/edge to ^0.9.3 (we patched redirect handling)
- ensure your CORS preflight adds `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`
- if you must support the iframe flow with third-party cookie blockers, consider sending the API key via a SameSite=None Secure cookie or via a short-lived session token from your server (avoid exposing the raw API key in the browser).

lara: I'll backport a clearer error message when Authorization is missing after a redirect in the next patch so these show up as "auth-strip-on-redirect" in logs instead of the generic 401.

zoe: Thanks — will try upgrade + CORS header fix and update the ticket with results.

eng-kiana: If the customer can't upgrade immediately, we can provide a tiny server-side proxy snippet (5 lines) that preserves headers and handles redirect manually. Ping me and I'll drop it in the ticket. :+1:
